newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease modestly on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease modestly on fund selling.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures eased modestly late Monday on fund liquidation but futher losses were seen limited, dealers said.
Recent weakness in Japan's stock market, with the Nikkei 225 testing 18,300-point support on Monday, reinforced market views that low-interest rates would be maintained in the mid-term.
The recovery in the Nikkei 225 cash market in mid-afternoon partly reduced buying interest in Euroyen, but the contract was supported by views Japan's economy was in a bearish mode.
"The BOJ (Bank of Japan) maintaining a low interest policy will keep support coming back," a Japanese house dealer said.
December Euroyen was quoted at 99.19 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.20, off from an intraday high of 99.22.
Dealers said the brief spurt was a function of hedge funds speculating in dollar/yen, which saw the dollar recoup losses against the yen in late action on Asian currency markets.
JGB's were lacklustre, trading narrowly within a 25-tick range awaiting the rollover of the key March contract into June, and with the dollar clawing back to 120 yen dampening demand.
March JGBs hit a peak of 126.52 before coming off to finish at 126.31 against their previous 126.34, with the downside minimised by short covering.
September JGB's stagnated at 124.82 against 124.83, failing to sustain highs at 125.06.
Eurodollars ended weaker in thin trade hamstrung by concerns over a U.S. rate hike after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments about a need to check inflation last week.
Dealers said sentiment was defensive ahead of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on March 5, and U.S. jobs data later this week, which were likely to show a more robust economy.
September Eurodollars finished weaker at 93.98 against their IMM close at 94.00 on volume of 9,630 lots.
